narrative:
The model estimates a 60% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your total years of experience across all jobs stands out as the strongest factor pushing the model toward expecting you to leave. At 6-10 years, you fall into a group that the model associates with higher turnover compared to the majority of employees it predicts will stay, who more often have only 1-5 years of overall experience. Similarly, the length of time you have spent in your current role (1-5 years) is the second most influential factor and also pulls the prediction toward leaving. Employees the model expects to stay tend to have either much shorter or longer tenures here, making your mid-range duration a notable risk signal.

The third important element actually works in your favor: you have not received other job offers while at this company. This lack of external opportunities pushes the prediction back toward staying and helps moderate the overall risk.

Taken together, your experience profile signals to the model that you may be at a natural transition point in your career. The organization should discuss your long-term goals with you and explore whether additional responsibilities, clearer advancement paths, or adjusted compensation could increase your sense of stability. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel like the right choice at this stage.
